questions.q: What is the Report Server service?
options: The Windows service that hosts the Report Server web service and runs background processing
A database that stores report snapshots
A browser-based UI for browsing report content
A stand-alone report authoring application
questions.explain: The Report Server service is the Windows service at the center of a native-mode installation — it hosts the web service and handles background processing like scheduled operations and delivery.

questions.q: What is the Report Server web service actually responsible for?
options: It's the real communications interface between client programs (the web portal, Report Builder, SSDT) and the report server
It's a caching layer with no client-facing role
It only handles email subscription delivery
It replaces the need for a report server database
questions.explain: Every tool that talks to the report server — the web portal, Report Builder, SSDT, scripted tools — goes through the Report Server web service.

questions.q: Why does a native-mode report server use two databases (ReportServer and ReportServerTempDB) instead of one?
options: To separate persistent data (reports, schedules, history, security) from temporary data (session data, cached reports, work tables)
ReportServerTempDB is just a backup copy of ReportServer
One database is for SharePoint mode only and is never used in native mode
SQL Server requires every application to use exactly two databases
questions.explain: ReportServer stores everything that must survive a restart; ReportServerTempDB stores session data, cached reports, and work tables that don't need to persist and are periodically cleaned up.

questions.q: Which statement about the web portal is correct?
options: It's the browser-based front end for browsing, running, and administering content, and it's only available in native mode
It's a Windows service, not a browser interface
It's available identically whether the report server runs in native mode or SharePoint-integrated mode
It replaces the Report Server web service entirely
questions.explain: The web portal is built on top of the web service and is available only when the report server runs in native mode — not when it's integrated with SharePoint.

questions.q: What's the key difference between the web service's default URL and the web portal's default URL?
options: The web service uses a virtual directory like /reportserver (machine-facing); the web portal uses one like /reports (human-facing)
They are always the exact same URL
The web portal has no URL at all — it only opens from Report Server Configuration Manager
The web service URL is only used in SharePoint mode
questions.explain: By default the report server's virtual directory is something like /reportserver, while the web portal uses a different virtual directory such as /reports — mixing the two up is a common early mistake.
